The arrest was also confirmed by the country’s interior minister, Marcin Kierwiński. properties.article_text_excerpt: A police car leaving RAF Molesworth after the two men were arrested. Photograph: Chris Radburn/Reuters View image in fullscreen A police car leaving RAF Molesworth after the two men were arrested. Photograph: Chris Radburn/Reuters UK news Two Latvian men arrested at RAF base in Cambridgeshire used by US military Men aged 32 and 36 detained on suspicion of trespass, causing criminal damage and entering a prohibited place Dan Sabbagh Defence and security editor Thu 8 Oct 2026 17.27 EDT First published on Thu 8 Oct 2026 11.53 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Two Latvian men were arrested in the early hours of Thursday after they were discovered inside the perimeter of RAF Molesworth, a Cambridgeshire base used by the US military and Nato for intelligence operations. The men, 32 and 36, were picked up at 2am inside the base, in an investigation that began four hours earlier when military police discovered an abandoned vehicle outside the facility. Military police, helped by officers from Cambridgeshire police, discovered a small hole in the perimeter fence before finding and arresting the men, initially on suspicion of trespass on a prohibited site and causing criminal damage.
